pattern.short_summary: A continuous artifact is partitioned into named units, and each unit becomes an independently addressable object.
pattern.definition: A continuous artifact is partitioned into named units, and each unit becomes an independently addressable object. Operations that would otherwise apply to the whole — editing, regenerating, tagging, attributing — apply per unit. The partition is materialized on screen, and its boundaries may themselves be adjustable.
pattern.structural_signature: A single artifact is divided into a set of non-overlapping parts, each given an identity (a name, a type label, a card, a row). Each part carries its own handles, so the artifact has as many operation targets as it has parts, all simultaneously present. Segmentation may be automatic or user-adjusted, but the resulting units persist as the unit of interaction rather than dissolving back into the whole.

dimension.category_description: How users inspect, modify, scope, revise, accept, program, or interrupt generated work at the artifact level.
dimension.classification_boundary: Centers user control during or after generation, including editable intermediate generators and representations.
